request.lesson: Stasis detection is the wrong convergence signal for an iterated spec review. loop-cohort's matches_previous_round fires only when the SAME findings recur; across four pre-EXECUTE rounds on a 157-criterion contract it returned false every time while a majority of each round's sustained findings were defects the previous round's amendment had introduced. The signal that distinguishes progress from churn is the repair-induced fraction: what share of sustained findings cite text the last amendment changed. It is mechanically computable from the prior diff and the findings' line citations. Arm it at roughly half for two consecutive rounds.

Spec amendments divide into two classes that behave completely differently under review. Corrections to existing text - narrowing an overclaim, scoping a criterion, repointing a citation, fixing a count, aligning gate lists - were sustained once and never recurred across four rounds. Every amendment that ADDED a new control to close a gap produced findings in the next round, and one handed an inspected repository influence over which process groups the application would signal. Closing a gap at a trust boundary is design work: it needs a decision about where state lives, who owns it, and what happens when its integrity fails. Writing one criterion inside a review loop looks like the same act and is not. When a sustained finding asks for a new control rather than a correction, check whether several findings are one design question wearing different hats, and hand that question back as one item instead of drafting criteria under review pressure.

Route every reviewer claim through finding adjudication before stating it as fact, including in a conversational summary. Across one run three claims were reported as established and then refuted: an axis-basis mismatch resolved by the spec's own precedence rule, a repair-induced attribution count, and a collapsed verdict-by-condition product that a criterion's totality made constructible. The adjudication gateway was honoured for every persisted artifact and bypassed for every narration, which is backwards - the narration is where the reader forms their picture. Reading source lines directly is not a substitute: one boundary-violation claim rested on four lines that were each true and a fifth, unread, that resolved it. Adjudication is exhaustive over the supplied authority set; an opportunistic read is not.

Supersedes the earlier claim that spec corrections do not recur while added controls do. Measured over five pre-EXECUTE rounds, a corrections-only round produced the best result of the run - sustained findings fell 9 to 5 and blockers 2 to 1 - so the discipline works, but about 80 percent of what it did produce were still defects the round's own amendments caused. The distinction that actually predicts recurrence is not whether an edit adds a criterion or restates one; it is whether the edit changes what the criterion OBLIGES. Three edits classified as corrections were semantic widenings in a correction's clothing: one took a criterion from naming two surfaces to asserting a class over every surface, one added a positive mandate where the criterion had only excluded a value, and one created a discriminator no criterion supplied a source for. Classify an amendment by its effect on the obligation, not by its form, and when an edit widens an obligation walk every sibling criterion that shares its taxonomy in the same action.
